_about: Rows of the v2 hand test (PLAN-021 WP-G). Only what needs a person, a real model or this computer's own fonts; everything CI or tools/layout_check_script.py can measure is not here. Each row starts from a stated state, never from another row. A row is added in the same pull request as the fix it checks. {version} is read from metadata.txt when the bundle is built.

rows.title: Update in place, then untick and tick the plugin during a request
rows.starts_from: QGIS with the previous Cartogen AI version installed and a project open (any project)
rows.do: Follow 'Updating an existing install' in README_FIRST.txt to install 1_plugin/cartogen_ai_v{version}.zip over the installed one, restart QGIS twice, then send any short request (for example: how many layers are in the project?) and, while it runs, untick Cartogen AI in Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins > Installed and tick it again.
rows.expect: Help shows Version {version}; one toolbar button, one Plugins menu entry, one Cartogen panel; no red lines in the CartogenAI log tab; unticking during the request leaves no error and ticking again gives one button, one entry, one panel.
rows.evidence: Screenshot of the toolbar and Help after the update; the Log Messages CartogenAI tab saved as a text file

rows.title: Stop a long processing request; memory comes back
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_boundary and smoke_points loaded from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Note QGIS's memory in the operating system's task manager. Send: Create 300000 random points inside smoke_boundary and add to each the distance to the nearest point of smoke_points. Press Stop in the panel after a few seconds. Watch the memory for a minute. Then send: how many layers are in the project?
rows.expect: The panel says it stopped; no output layer is added; memory does not stay high; the next request works.
rows.evidence: The memory figure before, at the peak and a minute after Stop (write the three numbers in the notes)
rows.needs: person and the operating system's task manager

rows.title: Contour lines of a loaded DEM do not start a download
rows.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_dem.tif added as a raster layer (Layer > Add Layer > Add Raster Layer) and renamed to dem
rows.do: Send: draw contour lines of the dem every 100
rows.expect: A new line layer of contours appears (the reply names it and the file). The assistant does NOT call fetch_dem or run_steps (the evidence folder shows the tools). The reply says where the file is, and says so when it is in the temporary folder.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the Layers panel
rows.prompt: draw contour lines of the dem every 100

rows.title: 'animate the layer over time' runs the animation tool, not a how-to
rows.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_events.csv added through Layer > Add Layer > Add Delimited Text Layer (X field lon, Y field lat, geometry point, CRS EPSG:4326)
rows.do: Send: make the layer smoke_events temporal using the date field. Then, in the same chat, send: animate the layer over time
rows.expect: The second request calls export_temporal_animation_frames and reports the frames it wrote; it does not answer with instructions for doing it by hand.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request

rows.title: Elevation profile in a layout is added, not looked up again and again
rows.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_dem.tif renamed to dem and smoke_roads from 3_test_files/smoke_network.gpkg; first send: create a print layout of the map called Test Layout
rows.do: Send: Turn on elevation for the dem, then draw an elevation profile along the road in Test Layout
rows.expect: The dem has elevation turned on and the layout holds an elevation profile item along the road. list_layout_items is called at most twice and fetch_dem is not called.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the layout
rows.prompt: draw an elevation profile along the road

rows.title: Charts linked to maps become layout charts, not an HTML dashboard
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_admin from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg; first send: create a print layout of the map called Test Layout
rows.do: Send: Produce charts linked to maps in Test Layout
rows.expect: A chart item is added to the layout (add_layout_chart); no HTML dashboard is written.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the layout

rows.title: 'Combine two layers into one' is a merge, not an imagery plan
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_points and smoke_hubs from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Send: Combine the layers smoke_points and smoke_hubs into one layer.
rows.expect: A merge runs and a merged layer is added. No satellite imagery search or feature extraction is started.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request
rows.prompt: Combine the layers smoke_points and smoke_hubs into one layer

rows.title: 'Convert to a raster with the population in each cell' is not a WorldPop plan
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_admin from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Send: Convert smoke_admin to a raster with the population in each cell.
rows.expect: A rasterise algorithm runs on smoke_admin using its population field; fetch_worldpop_population is not called.
rows.evidence: The evidence folder of the request
rows.prompt: Convert smoke_admin to a raster with the population in each cell

rows.title: Undo of add_field: an empty new column goes, a filled one stays
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_points from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Send: add a text field called notes to smoke_points. Then send: undo that. (Confirm the undo card.) Then send: add a text field called notes to smoke_points again, then: set notes to 'checked' for every feature, then: undo the last operation.
rows.expect: After the first undo the field notes is gone from the attribute table. After the second add and fill, undo does not remove it: the reply says the field now holds values and nothing was changed, and the values are still there.
rows.evidence: The evidence folders of the requests; a screenshot of the attribute table after each undo
rows.prompt: add a text field called notes to smoke_points

rows.title: Result checks are recorded on a computed layer, and switch off with the setting
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened (QGIS closed and reopened since the last row), Cartogen panel open, a new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked
rows.do: Send in the chat: Calculate a severity index for the three polygons in smoke_admin using its numeric population and need fields, with admin_name as the unit name. Use equal weights and write the score to severity_smoke. Approve the preview. Then snap('W1a'). Then, in the console: from qgis.core import QgsSettings; QgsSettings().setValue('cartogen_ai/result_gate', False); open a NEW chat and send: Recalculate the severity index for smoke_admin into a field called severity_two. Approve. Then snap('W1b'). Set it back with QgsSettings().setValue('cartogen_ai/result_gate', True).
rows.expect: W1a: the reply states how many checks ran and, when any failed or were weak, names them in its own words (it may not say 'all fine' over a failed check). W1b: no new check run is recorded and the reply carries no check statement.
rows.evidence: evidence/W1a and evidence/W1b (from snap), each with layer_properties.json, steps.jsonl, window.png; the chat text pasted into notes
rows.prompt: Calculate a severity index for the three polygons in smoke_admin
rows.outputs: field severity_smoke, then severity_two, on smoke_admin; no files
rows.pass_if: W1a layer_properties.json: smoke_admin has key cartogen/checks with at least 1 run. W1b: its run list is unchanged in length (still the W1a runs). Judge the reply wording by eye.

rows.title: A fetched layer gets result checks and a source record
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened (QGIS closed and reopened since the last row), Cartogen panel open, a new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked; internet available
rows.do: Send: Fetch the admin level 1 boundaries for Yemen from geoBoundaries. Then snap('W2').
rows.expect: A new layer appears. Its record holds the source name, URL, licence, date fetched and coverage; the licence line says the licence was NOT checked against the provider. Result checks were recorded.
rows.evidence: evidence/W2 (layer_properties.json, layers.txt, window.png, steps.jsonl)
rows.prompt: Fetch the admin level 1 boundaries for Yemen from geoBoundaries
rows.pass_if: layer_properties.json for the new layer has cartogen/sources (name, url, licence, licence_checked=false, fetched date) and cartogen/checks.

rows.title: The provenance record and the spatial report print the data source
rows.starts_from: a project with internet: any project (the first message fetches the layer), new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked
rows.do: Send: Fetch the admin level 1 boundaries for Yemen from geoBoundaries. Then: Show me the provenance record of that layer. Then: Generate a spatial report titled Source check with one insight: the Yemen boundaries come from geoBoundaries. Then snap('W3').
rows.expect: The record lists the source name, URL, licence, date and coverage, and says the licence was not checked. The report file has a 'Data source:' line for the layer.
rows.evidence: evidence/W3; the report file copied to results/outputs/W3/
rows.outputs: one new layer and a spatial report file (path is in the reply)
rows.pass_if: Open the report: it contains 'Data source:' and the word geoBoundaries and does not say the licence was verified.

rows.title: The verified workflow report lists failed checks first, sources, ordered steps and gaps
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened (QGIS closed and reopened since the last row), Cartogen panel open, a new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked
rows.do: Send: Buffer smoke_points by 500 metres and call the result smoke_reach. Then: Join smoke_reach to smoke_zones by location (spatial_join), call it smoke_reach_joined. Then: Write a workflow report titled Smoke reach for smoke_reach_joined. Then snap('W4').
rows.expect: A Markdown report is written. Order inside it: failed checks first, then data sources, then the steps in the order they ran with their real arguments, then assumptions and limitations including every gap (layers never checked, origin unknown).
rows.evidence: evidence/W4; the report copied to results/outputs/W4/
rows.prompt: Write a workflow report titled Smoke reach
rows.pass_if: The .md has the buffer step before the join step; 500 appears as the distance; a layer with no recorded check is named as unchecked; nothing in it is a figure the plugin did not record.

rows.title: HDX search puts the open, recent, in-country data set first and explains why
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened (QGIS closed and reopened since the last row), Cartogen panel open, a new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked; internet available
rows.do: Send: find a dataset of health facilities in Yemen. Then snap('W5'). Open the first result's HDX page in a browser and compare.
rows.expect: The first result is open-licensed, recently changed and lists Yemen; each 'why' line matches its HDX page (licence, last change, country). A data set that states no licence says so instead of being called open.
rows.evidence: evidence/W5; a screenshot of the first result's HDX page saved as results/screens/W5-hdx.png
rows.prompt: find a dataset of health facilities in Yemen
rows.outputs: a ranked list in the reply
rows.pass_if: Three facts checked against the HDX page of result 1: licence, last-modified date, country. Write all three in notes with the page values.

rows.title: MCP server refuses wrong token, Host and Origin, and lists only reviewed tools (script, no model)
rows.starts_from: QGIS with smoke_start.qgz open. smoke_points is untouched. For P5 first mark smoke_zones SENSITIVE (chat: mark smoke_zones as SENSITIVE because test, approve).
rows.do: Plugins > Cartogen AI > MCP server (local)..., accept the warning, copy the address and token from the dialog. In a terminal (not QGIS): python mcp_probe.py <ADDRESS> <TOKEN> results/outputs/W6 --layer smoke_points --sensitive-layer smoke_zones. Then choose the menu item again to stop the server and run the same command once more.
rows.expect: All checks print PASS (P1a-c, P2a-c, P3, P4a-b, P5). After stopping the server the second run cannot connect (status 0).
rows.evidence: results/outputs/W6/mcp_probe.json and mcp_probe.md; the terminal output; a screenshot of the 'MCP server running' dialog without the token visible
rows.inputs: the running server's address and token
rows.pass_if: python tools/check_evidence.py shows no FAIL for this row; mcp_probe.json 'checks' all ok=true; a tools/list reply with fewer than 24 tools or any of execute_pyqgis_script, delete_layer is a FAIL.

rows.title: A write over MCP asks first: Deny, Allow once, timeout and SENSITIVE (person at the dialog)
rows.starts_from: As W6, server running, smoke_zones NOT sensitive for this row; a terminal with mcp_probe.py
rows.do: Run: python mcp_probe.py <ADDRESS> <TOKEN> results/outputs/W7 --write-tool-check --wait-for-person. It sends a buffer_analysis call. When the dialog appears press DENY; repeat leaving it for 2 minutes. Then use Claude Code or the probe's raw call (see the guide, section MCP) to send buffer_analysis on smoke_points distance 500 output_name mcp_allowed and press ALLOW ONCE. Finally mark smoke_points SENSITIVE and send it again: no dialog may appear.
rows.expect: The dialog names buffer_analysis, says it is a change (CREATE) and shows the arguments exactly as sent; Deny and the timeout both come back as not run and make no layer; Allow once makes layer mcp_allowed; on a SENSITIVE layer the call is refused with no dialog.
rows.evidence: mcp_probe.json for each attempt; a screenshot of the dialog itself (results/screens/W7-dialog.png); a screenshot of the layers panel after each outcome
rows.outputs: layer mcp_allowed only after Allow once; mcp_probe.json
rows.pass_if: No layer named mcp_probe_should_not_exist or created by a denied/timed-out call exists; exactly one new layer (mcp_allowed) exists after the whole row; the dialog text is readable by a non-technical person (write one line on what confused you).

rows.title: Export a workflow file: preview first, then a file with no data, paths or credentials
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened, a new chat, 'Save an evidence folder for each request' ticked
rows.do: Send: Buffer smoke_points by 500 metres and call the result smoke_reach. Then: Join smoke_reach to smoke_zones by location, call it smoke_reach_joined. Then: Export the workflow that made smoke_reach_joined as a file called Smoke reach. Read the preview card (steps, roles, nothing skipped without a reason), say yes. Copy the saved .cgworkflow.json to results/outputs/W8/. Then snap('W8').
rows.expect: A preview card appears BEFORE any file exists; after confirming, one file is written. Roles name the starting layers (smoke_points, smoke_zones); no path, no coordinates, no key.
rows.evidence: evidence/W8; results/outputs/W8/<file>.cgworkflow.json; a screenshot of the preview card (results/screens/W8-preview.png)
rows.prompt: Export the workflow that made smoke_reach_joined
rows.pass_if: python check_workflow_file.py results/outputs/W8/<file> --expect-valid exits 0 (accepted, no LEAK line). Its steps are buffer_analysis then spatial_join, in that order.

rows.title: Open a workflow file: read the dialog, map the role, run, and the result is traceable to the file
rows.starts_from: the copied smoke_start.qgz freshly opened; the file smoke_reach.cgworkflow.json from 3_test_files
rows.do: Plugins > Cartogen AI > Open workflow file..., choose smoke_reach.cgworkflow.json. Read the dialog (warning, checksum, both steps). Map role 'points' to smoke_points. Press Run and watch the chat. Then snap('W9'). Then send: Show me the provenance record of hand_test_reach.
rows.expect: The dialog shows the file name, a checksum and both steps in plain words; Run is enabled only after the role is mapped. The chat runs buffer then count in order and ends with a count of 5. The provenance record mentions the workflow file's name and fingerprint.
rows.evidence: evidence/W9; a screenshot of the dialog (results/screens/W9-dialog.png); a screenshot of the chat after the run
rows.pass_if: layers.txt shows hand_test_reach with features=5; layer_properties.json lineage entry holds the fingerprint 181c6cbe04b1d60e268bbfd7df29ab8246170ebc6f326853cbcf7f5bf6b135ad (this equals python tools/check_workflow_file.py on the file).
rows.cost: model-free apart from the provenance question

rows.title: Six broken files are each refused in a plain sentence and nothing runs
rows.starts_from: smoke_start.qgz open, nothing from other rows required; the six bad_*.cgworkflow.json files from 3_test_files
rows.do: First, in a terminal: python check_workflow_file.py 3_test_files/bad_*.cgworkflow.json --expect-invalid --json results/outputs/W10/expected.json (this is the free pre-check and lists the sentence each file should give). Then open each of the six files with Plugins > Cartogen AI > Open workflow file... and write down the sentence the dialog shows.
rows.expect: Each file is refused with a sentence that says what is wrong (tool not allowed, a file path, more than 20 steps, a newer version, not valid JSON, unknown role). The dialog never offers Run. No layer is added.
rows.evidence: results/outputs/W10/expected.json; a screenshot per refusal named results/screens/W10-<filename>.png; layers.txt after the last one (snap('W10'))
rows.pass_if: The sentence in each screenshot matches the problem sentence in expected.json; layer_count in project.json is unchanged from the start.

rows.title: A workflow step that would send a RESTRICTED area stops at the usual card
rows.starts_from: smoke_start.qgz freshly opened; smoke_egress_stop.cgworkflow.json from 3_test_files
rows.do: Send in the chat: mark smoke_zones as RESTRICTED because test, approve. Then Open workflow file... smoke_egress_stop.cgworkflow.json, map role 'area' to smoke_zones, Run. Then snap('W11').
rows.expect: The run stops at the confirmation card the egress gate normally shows; nothing is sent to WorldPop and no layer is made. RECORD the exact card text: this behaviour has never been seen by a person.
rows.evidence: evidence/W11; screenshot of the card (results/screens/W11-card.png)
rows.pass_if: No new layer; steps.jsonl shows no completed fetch_worldpop_population; the card text is pasted into notes.

rows.title: A reader who has not seen the guide can follow docs/WORKFLOW_FILES.md
rows.starts_from: a person who did not write it, QGIS with smoke_start.qgz
rows.do: Give them docs/WORKFLOW_FILES.md only (in the bundle: 3_test_files\WORKFLOW_FILES.md). Ask them to export and open a file using the guide alone. Time them. Note every place they stop, guess or ask.
rows.expect: They finish without help. Each place they were stuck is written down as a sentence of the guide to change.
rows.evidence: a notes file results/outputs/W12/notes.txt: time taken, each stuck point, the guide line involved
rows.pass_if: Finished without asking anyone, or the stuck points are listed with the guide line number.
